assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible-terminator sequencing by synthesis turned a nucleotide-incorporation reaction into the workhorse of all genomics; the underlying chemistry (modified dNTPs, polymerase tolerance, surface clustering) is concrete and originates in nucleotide chemistry. Its consequences for genome stability, cancer and population genetics research are enormous, and I know first-hand how much our field depends on it.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa chemistry is credited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman (with Mayer's clustering and Ju's reversible-terminator work in parallel); Rothberg's pyrosequencing platform is a separate technological line. A fair three-person configuration is possible but excludes other genuine contributors.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of dominant use with unmistakable independent validation. Recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Which contributions (Solexa chemistry versus 454 pyrosequencing versus Ju's terminators) are chemically decisive is contested.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as instrumentation and biology; my recollection of the detailed priority history is imperfect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors fuse an engineered deaminase to a catalytically impaired Cas protein, converting one base into another on DNA without double-strand cleavage. This is a clear, chemically defined reaction that gave biologists a general tool and has reached the clinic. I value that the mechanism was designed and the editing outcome measured quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: David Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead postdoc inventors of the cytosine and adenine editors. A single-laureate award to Liu is defensible; adding the two trainees would be unusual.
assessment.maturity: Seven to ten years since the first reports, with extensive independent replication and first clinical results. The chemistry is mature, though long-term safety, off-target deamination and bystander editing data are still accumulating.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges base editing as chemistry or as genome engineering following the CRISPR prize.
Long-term clinical outcomes are not yet known.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking ubiquitin ligases with bifunctional molecules or molecular glues to remove proteins is a new chemical modality, and the mechanism of thalidomide acting through cereblon explains a long-standing drug mystery. The concept converts occupancy-based pharmacology into event-driven catalytic degradation, with substantial biomedical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made major contributions to VHL ligands, structure and drugs, so any selection is contentious. The list has up to eight credited names and the allocation is truly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in trials but approvals are lacking, so the therapeutic proof remains incomplete. The basic chemical principle is well confirmed by many groups.
uncertainties: Division of credit between PROTAC inventors and molecular-glue mechanism discoverers.
No approved degrader drug yet, so timing may be early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase pairs allow site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells, effectively adding chemistry to the genetic code. It gave chemists and biologists a general tool to install probes, crosslinkers and new functionality into proteins, and it later expanded to reprogrammed codons and ribosomes.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial systems; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama have strong secondary claims. A three-person division looks fair but not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent use in many labs; the technique is established, and applications continue to broaden.
uncertainties: Priority among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama for specific advances.
Whether the committee sees broad enough use compared with other chemical biology candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that mRNA carries a reversible, enzymatically regulated methylation (writers, erasers, readers) opened epitranscriptomics. The FTO demethylation finding gave a concrete chemical reaction with biological meaning, and the transcriptome-wide maps showed the distribution of the mark. Links to cancer and development are clearly relevant.
assessment.attribution: Jia and He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and framed reversibility; Rechavi/Dominissini and Jaffrey/Meyer independently mapped the modification. Yang and others contributed on the writer and reader side. The decisive contributions are shared and allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mapping methods have faced reproducibility and antibody-specificity concerns, and the field is still debating stoichiometry and functional significance at individual sites. That is the kind of issue I take seriously, so I treat maturity as moderate.
uncertainties: Reproducibility and quantification of m6A maps; antibody cross-reactivity (for example with m6Am).
Disputed physiological role of FTO as an m6A demethylase.
Complex allocation across more than three groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic acid sequence by the ionic current through a single pore is a genuinely chemical-physical measurement concept, realized in portable long-read sequencers with direct detection of modified bases, including those relevant to genome maintenance. The engineering of pore proteins and motor enzymes by Bayley and colleagues is chemistry in a major role.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Church conceived the idea; Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Bayley engineered the pores; Akeson showed enzymatic control. Credit is distributed and the configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices have been used widely for roughly a decade and independent replication is strong, but accuracy and application scope are still developing.
uncertainties: Fair split between conception, demonstration, pore engineering and motor control.
Whether the committee finds this adequately chemistry compared with sequencing by synthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation methods made solution structure and dynamics of proteins of substantial size accessible, including mechanisms of enzymes and conformational exchange. Chemical shift and relaxation measurements are quantitative and widely reproduced; this is measurement-driven chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay are leaders in methods development, with Wagner and Palmer as other substantial contributors. A trio is plausible, but the Wüthrich prize of 2002 already recognized the original structure determination, so novelty relative to that award needs thought.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with decades of confirmation, perhaps with diminishing urgency as cryo-EM and prediction methods overtake it.
uncertainties: Relative standing with respect to cryo-EM and computed structures today.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyses N2 reduction with a complex metal cofactor, and structures (including the interstitial carbide in FeMoco) and spectroscopic/kinetic work have clarified electron delivery and substrate binding. As an enzymologist I value the effort to define a mechanism for a metalloenzyme with radical-like intermediates, but the catalytic mechanism is still not fully resolved.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first structure, cofactor and states), Einsle (carbide, high-resolution structures) and Seefeldt/Dean (mechanistic and genetic work) all made decisive contributions; Ribbe is also prominent. The configuration is plausible but excludes some who made major advances.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the mechanism of N2 binding and reduction remains incomplete, so recognition might be premature relative to the strongest parts of the story.
uncertainties: Unresolved mechanism of N2 reduction at the cofactor.
